predecessors.name: Kingdom of Sardinia
predecessors.text: Piedmont and Aosta, the mainland of Charles Emmanuel IV's Kingdom of Sardinia under French occupation

successors.name: French Consulate
successors.text: the departements of Doire, Marengo, Pô, Sesia, Stura and Tanaro: Piedmont and Aosta without Novara

successors.name: Italian Republic (Kingdom of Italy from 1805)
successors.text: Novara, annexed as the department of Agogna

ledger.x: December 1798: the French occupy Turin and the Piedmontese Republic replaces the king's mainland rule.
20 June 1799: Austro-Russian troops end the Piedmontese Republic.
11 September 1802: Piedmont and Aosta become French departements.
11 September 1802: Novara goes to the Italian Republic.

wars.name: Second Italian campaign of 1799-1800 in Piedmont
wars.outcome: Austro-Russian troops conquered the Piedmontese Republic on 20 June 1799; Napoleon returned to Italy in 1800 and the republic was re-established on 20 June 1800 ('Napoleon returned to Italy, taking back much of the new republics').

certainty.note: The page names the territory of Piedmont but no boundary; the six departements of 1802 are the only named subdivisions.
